formulas.name: Block density (White, Boorman and Breiger 1976)
formulas.where: Mean tie value from block \(r\) to block \(s\) over the possible pairs of distinct nodes (a binary \(x\) gives the proportion of present ties). Defined when the block pair has at least one possible pair: not for a block of one node on the diagonal (\(n_r^2-n_r=0\)).

formulas.name: Block density counting loops
formulas.where: When loops are possible ties the diagonal pairs are included; defined for \(n_r\ge1\).

variants.block_density: The matrix \((d_{rs})\) of block densities for a given partition: ties over possible pairs per ordered pair of blocks, diagonal excluded (loop-inclusive and valued forms use the second formula or the mean tie value).

edge_cases.definition_gives: A single node is one block of size 1: its diagonal block has no possible pair, so \(d_{11}\) is 0/0: not defined.
A partition into more blocks than nodes allow leaves empty blocks: undefined cells (0/0).
An empty block has \(n_r=0\): every cell involving it is 0/0; a block with one node has an undefined diagonal.
Excluded from the first formula (\(j\ne i\)); included in the second.
With a binary \(x\) parallel edges count once; with a valued \(x\) the weight is the total.
\(d_{rs}\) and \(d_{sr}\) differ for directed data; undirected data give a symmetric matrix.
Valued ties give the mean tie value instead of the proportion.
Every cell is 1 (diagonal cells of single-node blocks excepted).

formulas.name: CONCOR (Breiger, Boorman and Arabie 1975)
formulas.where: Iterated correlation converges to a matrix of entries \(\pm1\); the nodes are split into two blocks by the sign pattern, and each block is split again by repeating the procedure on its submatrix. A column with zero variance makes the correlation 0/0.

variants.concor: Blocks obtained by repeated splitting by iterated correlation, numbered from 1; the formula above is the iteration step.

formulas.where: Coreness is chosen to maximize the Pearson correlation between observed ties and the pattern \(c_ic_j\) over distinct pairs. The correlation is 0/0 when the ties or the pattern are constant (an empty or complete graph, or constant \(c\)).

formulas.where: Least-squares fit of the rank-one pattern to the off-diagonal adjacency entries; unique up to sign, with the sign fixed by non-negativity.

formulas.name: Automorphic equivalence
formulas.where: Two nodes are equivalent when some automorphism (tie-preserving permutation) maps one to the other; the classes are the orbits of the automorphism group. Orbit computation by canonical labelling is due to McKay and Piperno 2014. Every orbit is a union of structural-equivalence classes and lies inside a regular-equivalence class.

variants.automorphic_equivalence: The orbit label of each node under the automorphism group of the binary (or multiplicity-valued) ties.

A loop is preserved by an automorphism: nodes with and without loops are in different orbits.
Multiplicities are part of the structure: \(a_{\varphi(u)\varphi(v)}=a_{uv}\).

edge_cases.definition_gives: For directed graphs \(a_{ij}\) is not symmetric, so fewer permutations are automorphisms.

formulas.name: Regular equivalence (White and Reitz 1983)
formulas.latex: i\equiv j\Rightarrow\begin{cases}\forall k:\,a_{ik}=1\Rightarrow\exists l:\,a_{jl}=1,\ l\equiv k\\ \forall k:\,a_{ki}=1\Rightarrow\exists l:\,a_{lj}=1,\ l\equiv k\end{cases}
formulas.where: An equivalence relation is regular when equivalent nodes have ties to and from equivalent nodes. The relation is not unique: the coarsest (all nodes) is always regular, so a procedure fixes the one it reports (for example the maximal regular relation refining a seed partition, as the CATREGE iteration yields).

variants.regular_equivalence: The classes of the regular equivalence found by the tool (sna: classes at distance 0 of the CATREGE dissimilarity, optionally from a seed partition).
variants.cat_automorphic_catrege_equivalence_max_: Documented as the UCINET REGE and CATREGE regular-equivalence similarity procedures and Max Sim for automorphic equivalence; not recorded in detail.

formulas.name: Classical scaling (Torgerson 1952)
formulas.where: The first \(p\) eigenvectors scaled by the square roots of the \(p\) largest positive eigenvalues of \(B\). The configuration is unique up to rotation, reflection and sign, and is not determined when leading eigenvalues coincide.

formulas.name: Kruskal stress-1 (Kruskal 1964)
formulas.where: Non-metric scaling chooses \(X\) to minimize stress, where \(f\) is a monotone transformation of the dissimilarities; iterative, so the result depends on the start and may be a local minimum.

variants.classical_mds: Classical (Torgerson) scaling: eigendecomposition of the double-centred squared distance matrix.
variants.mds_nonmetric: Non-metric scaling that minimizes Kruskal's stress-1 over configurations and monotone transformations.

formulas.where:

e g(i)\)), representative (\(g(i)=g(j)
e g(k)\)), liaison (all three different); the total is \(\sum_R w_R(j)=|T_j|\). Counts are defined for every node and are 0 when no two-path exists.
